title: Mathis Albert, 16, surpasses Reyna, Pulisic as Bundesliga’s youngest American
content:
Mathis Albert surpassed Giovanni Reyna as the youngest American to play in the Bundesliga when he debuted for Borussia Dortmund on Sunday.

Albert, who hails from Greenville, South Carolina, was introduced in the 88th-minute of Dortmund’s win over Freiburg in the German top flight – aged 16 years, 11 months and 5 days.

He beat the record previously set by Reyna, who made his Bundesliga debut for Dortmund at 17 years, 2 months and 5 days on January 18, 2020.

Christian Pulisic drops to third on the list, having made his own Bundesliga bow for Dortmund on January 30, 2016, at 17 years, 4 months and 12 days.

Albert joined Dortmund’s academy from LA Galaxy’s youth program in 2024 and he was part of Dortmund’s senior roster at last summer’s Club World Cup in the U.S. He was the second youngest player at the tournament but did not make it off the bench as Dortmund were beaten by Real Madrid in the quarter-finals.

At international level, Albert was part of the U.S. team at last year’s Under-17 World Cup, and has since featured at U-19 level.

Goals from Maximilian Beier, Serhou Guirassy and Ramy Bensebaini put Dortmund in complete control inside the first half hour, before substitute Fabio Silva completed the scoring late on. The result assured Dortmund a place in the Bundesliga top four and next season’s Champions League with three matches still to play.
